paper_title: Developing Story Case Studies of Generative AI's Use in Journalism
caption: : The distribution of different input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs, over the WildChat conversations that are matched to online articles from the two identified news agencies.
model_annotation: The donut chart, titled “Stimulus Type,” illustrates the proportional distribution of various types of input material journalists provided to large language models (LLMs) during WildChat conversations that were matched to published articles from two news agencies. The chart is segmented into nine distinct categories, each represented by a different color and labeled with its corresponding percentage. The largest segment is “Draft/Other” at 26.4%, followed by “Press Release” at 18.7% and “External News Article” at 18.1%. Smaller segments include “Interview” (8.8%), “Organizational Report” (7.7%), “Event Posting” (6.6%), “Organizational Website” (4.9%), and “Intra-agency news article” (4.9%). The smallest segments are “Email” (2.7%) and “Social Media Post” (1.1%). Each slice is clearly labeled with its category name and percentage, positioned adjacent to the corresponding segment, and the central white space contains the chart’s title. The segments are arranged in a clockwise direction starting from the top-right, with no apparent ordering by size. The visual design allows for easy comparison of the relative proportions of stimulus types used in journalistic LLM interactions.
